The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 25.10.2022.
2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 25.10.2022 at about 3.00 p.m., petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider in a Bullet bearing No. KA-03-JK-1831 ridden by its rider slowly and cautiously, proceeding on Bandapura Medrich company, near Avalahalli- Budigere cross road, Bidarahalli Hobli, Bangalore, at that time Car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-ML-7539 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at a high speed and dashed to the bullet. Due to the sudden impact, the petitioner and rider fell down and sustained several grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Geetha Hospital for first aid treatment and thereafter shifted to Sundar Hospital, wherein she was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges, further he require one more surgery for removal of implants.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 58 years, the petitioner was a house wife. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner is not able to do job and hence lost her earnings. Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest. 
3. After service of notice, both the respondents have appeared before the Court through their counsels. But inspite of grant of sufficient opportunity, respondent No.2 not filed the written statement. 
The respondent No.1 filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. Further, this respondent submits that, at the time of alleged accident the driver was not holding Driving License to drive the vehicle. It Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/
2 is submitted that in reply, RTO Bengaluru has confirmed that the details of the said Driving License bearing DL No. KA05212240607 is not available with them. Further, the class of vehicle he is authorized to drive as per the said fake Driving License is abbreviated as 'MSWG' for the class of vehicle Motor Cycle with Gear, which otherwise is abbreviated as 'MCWG' by RTO's which itself suggests and substantiate that the Driving License is fabricated and a fake one. It is further submitted that, a police complaint has been lodged in this regard intimating the police that the Driving License produced by Shri. Bablukumar S/o Mahendra Puddari accused in Crime No.0415/2022 of Avalahalli Police Station, Hosakote Sub-Division, Bengaluru is a tampered and fake Driving License. It is furthe submitted that the 'B' Extract of the accused vehicle Car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-ML-7539 obtained by this respondent indicate the name of the accused shri.
Bablukumar S/o Mahendra Poddar as the owner of the vehicle . The accused intentionally has tampered the Driving License by creating a fake driving license to escape from liability to pay compensation. Further, this respondent is not a proper and a necessary party for adjudication of the claim. The petition is bad for misjoinder of party and the accused, the owner of the Car bearing Reg.
No. KA-05-ML-7539 as on the date of accident is a necessary party and is bad for non-joinder of party and the claim petition is liable to be dismissed. Further, this respondent accepts the issuance of policy inrespect of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-ML-7539 and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. 
The petitioner colluding with a owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 
4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 25-10-2022 at about 3.00 p.m., when she was proceeding as a pillion rider in a Bullet bearing Reg. No. KA-03-JK-1831 ridden by its rider slowly and cautiously by observing the movement of traffic and proceeding on Bandapura Medrich company near Avalahalli-Budigere cross road,
Bidarahalli Hobli, Bangalore, at that time one Car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-ML-7539 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life, without following traffic rules, came at high speed and dashed against motorcycle in which petitioner was proceeding and caused the accident, due to the forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained several grievous injuries as alleged by her?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom? 
3. What order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, she has got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.10 and also examined Dr. Nagaraj. B. N as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.11 and 12 and closed their side. On the other hand, one M. R. Girish,
Superintendent, RTO Jayanagar is examined as RW.1 and he got marked the documents at Ex.D1 and Ex.D2 and also examined Devaraj. C, retired ASI as RW.2 and he got marked the documents at Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/
3 Ex.D3 to Ex.D8 and also examined the authorized representative of the respondent No.1 company as RW.3 and he got marked the documents at Ex.D9 to Ex.D16.
6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record. 
7. My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the affirmative. 
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following: 
:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1: The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place she met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined herself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition. He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 9. As per the case of the petitioners, it could be seen that on 25.10.2022 at about 3.00 p.m., petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider in a Bullet bearing No. KA-03-JK-1831 ridden by its rider slowly and cautiously,
proceeding on Bandapura Medrich company, near Avalahalli-Budigere cross road, Bidarahalli Hobli, Bangalore, at that time Car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-ML-7539 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at a high speed and dashed to the bullet. Due to the sudden impact, the petitioner and rider fell down and sustained several grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. 
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Geetha Hospital for first aid treatment and thereafter shifted to Sundar Hospital, wherein she was treated as inpatient. Accordingly, the Avalahalli Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.415/2022. After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
10. Negligence is a specific tort and in any given circumstances, the failure to exercise that care which the circumstances demand, where there is a duty to exercise care, reasonable care must be taken to avoid acts or omissions which can be reasonably foreseen to be likely to cause physical injury to persons or property. In order to succeed in an action for damages/compensation for breach, the aggrieved must establish breach of statutory duty which on the construction of the statute. It is well settled that, those who claim negligence have to prove on the probabilities, as to whether breach or negligence, has caused or materially contributed to the damage suffered by the claimant/s.
11. The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person. It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others. In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act. 
Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/
4 Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something. In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do. 
12. The burden is upon the petitioners to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-ML-7539.
13. As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, " The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for " The Negligent Act ". 
14. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Avalahalli Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P2. On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 415/2022. The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P1.
15. During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.5 is the Charge-sheet,
Ex.P.6 is the Discharge summary, Ex.P7 is the Medical Bills, Ex.P8 is the Prescriptions, Ex.P.9 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card, Ex.P.10 is the IMV Report. Ex.P1 to 5 are the only documents, which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the Car driver. The Ex.P.3 (spot panchanama), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex-P5, Charge- Sheet against the driver of the Car U/s. 279, 337 and 338 of IPC. The Ex.P.10 i.e.,
certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question. 
16. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
17. The culpable negligence or rashness can be inferred from the attending circumstances like time of the accident, the width of the road and the nature of road etc. The Ex.P.3 is the spot Mahazar prepared by the Investigating Agency in the presence of panchas/ witnesses. As per charge-sheet at Ex.P5, FIR and First Information Statement i.e., Ex.P1 and Ex.P2, the driver of the Car drove his car in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle. Further, during the course of cross-examination respondent No.1 has not disputed the said accident and accident is caused due to the negligence of the rider of the two-wheeler. But it is not the case of the respondents that, they have challenged the charge-sheet filed by the I.O against respondent No.2. So, in such circumstances the defence taken by the respondent inrespect of negligence of the rider of the motorcycle is not tenable. Moreover, as stated above in a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required. On the other hand the petitioner has produced the sufficient documentary and oral evidences to prove that accident was due to rash and negligent Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/
5 driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-ML-7539 and resulted in grievous injuries to petitioner. Therefore, for the above stated reasons, I answer the Issue No.1 in affirmative. 
18. ISSUE No.2: The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident she was shifted to Geetha Hospital for first aid treatment and thereafter she was shifted to Sundar Hospital, wherein she was admitted as inpatient and took treatment. Petitioner has stated in the petition that, she is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. PAIN AND SUFFERING: In the petition as well as in his evidence PW1 deposed that, after the accident she was shifted to Sundar Hospital, wherein she treated as an inpatient from 25.10.2022 to 03.11.2022. The petitioner has produced the discharge card marked at Ex.P.6 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Sundar Hospital, Bangalore for 09 days. She has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.4. As per Wound certificate petitioner sustained fracture of superior margin of L1 vertebra, fracture of D2-D3-D4 vertebra spinous process. The doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature. Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience. Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering. 
20. MEDICAL EXPENSES: The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. In support of his plea, he has produced 13 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.7 to the tune of Rs.2,05,425/-. Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,05,425/-
towards medical expenses. 
21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD: The petitioner has produced Ex.P.6 Discharge summary issued by Sundar Hospital, Bengaluru, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 25.10.2022 to 03.11.2022 i.e. for 09 days. Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries. It is further contended that, the injured petitioner was a housewife. So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.15,500/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2022 at Rs.15,500/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka,
Bengaluru Bench. The accident is of the year is 2022. Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- p.m. as per above decision. Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income. Hence, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.31,000/- under this head. 
22. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability- The petitioner to prove her disability, she has produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj. B. N in order to substantiate the same, PW.2 who has opined that, total disability of whole body disability at 15%. 
Admittedly, the PW.2 is not a treated doctor. Same was admitted by the PW.2 during his cross examination, the relevant evidence of the PW.2 reads as follows :
Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/
6 "It is true to say that, I have not treated the petitioner personally." 
He was sworn that, petitioner has got 15% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate. It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability. However, looking to the nature of the injuries it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 9% of disability to the petitioner. 
23. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner/injured has to be determined. 
Ex.P.9 is the Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his D.O.B is mentioned as 25.06.1964 and accident took place in the year 2022. Accordingly, I assess her age as 58 years at the time of this accident. As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '09'. Hence Rs.15,500 X 12 X 9 X 9% = Rs.1,50,660/-. Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.1,50,660/-. 
24. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Sundar Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 25.10.2022 to 03.11.2022 i.e. for 09 days. Hence, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges. 
25. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS: The petitioner was aged about 58 years at the time of accident, she has sustained grievous injuries. It shows that she found difficulty in doing day to day works. She might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life. 
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.30,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness. 
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
2 Medical expenses Rs. 2,05,425/-
3 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 31,000/-
up period 4 Loss of future earning, Rs. 1,50,660/-
Disability 5 Nutritious food and Rs. 30,000/-
attendant charges 6 Loss of future amenities and Rs. 30,000/-
loss of happiness. 
Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/
7 Total Rs. 4,97,085/- 
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,97,085/- under various heads. 
26. LIABILITY: Learned counsel for the respondent No.1 vehemently argued that at the time of alleged accident the driver was not holding Driving License to drive the vehicle. It is submitted that in reply, RTO Bengaluru has confirmed that the details of the said Driving License bearing No.
KA05212240607 is not available with them. Further, the class of vehicle he is authorized to drive as per the said fake Driving License is abbreviated as 'MSWG' for the class of vehicle Motor Cycle with Gear, which otherwise is abbreviated as 'MCWG' by RTO's which itself suggests and substantiate that the Driving License is fabricated and a fake one. It is further submitted that, a police complaint has been lodged in this regard intimating the police that the Driving License produced by Shri. 
Bablukumar S/o Mahendra Puddari accused in Crime No.0415/2022 of Avalahalli Police Station,
Hosakote Sub-Division, Bengaluru is a tampered and fake Driving License. It is furthe submitted that the 'B' Extract of the accused vehicle Car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-ML-7539 obtained by this respondent indicate the name of the accused shri. Bablukumar S/o Mahendra Poddar as the owner of the vehicle. The accused intentionally has tampered the Driving License by creating a fake driving license to escape from liability to pay compensation. 
In this case, the I.O/police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle under section 279 and 338 of IPC and also adduced the evidence of the Superintendent, RTO Jayanagar as RW.1, Retired A.S.I as RW.2 and authorized person of respondent No.2 company as RW.3. RW.1 in his evidence deposed that, his office (RTO, Jayanagar) has not issued Driving License to Bablu Kumar who is driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-ML-7539. Further on perusal of the reply notice given by the Bablu Kumar at Ex.R7 it reveals that, the serial number of the Driving License is KA-05-212240607 and same is issued by the Jayanagar, Bangalore office, but as stated above RTO of Jayanagar, Bangalore himself present before this court and depose that, his office has not issued any such Driving License. Further, one person by name Bikram singh Rana RW.3 on behalf of insurance company i.e., Respondent No.1 adduced his evidence before this court and produced the insurance copy at Ex.R15 stating that, the vehicle involved in the accident is having insurance and at the same time he depose that, he has filed complaint before Halasur station in respect of creation of fake driving license against Bablu Kumar. The above discussion itself clear that, at the time of accident driver of the offending vehicle has not having driving license. 
No doubt, the Hon'ble Supreme court held that, in case of not having Driving License then the insurance company has to pay the compensation and then recover it from the owner of the vehicle. 
But the judgment of the Apex court in Beli Ram Vs. Rajinder Kumar and Another [AIR 2020 SC 4453] wherein the Apex Court observed as under:-
"Motor Vehicles Act (59 of 198), S.149 (2)(ao(ii), S.15 - Insurer's liability - Non-renewal of driving licence - Respondent - Claimant employed as driver met with accident while driving truck owned by employer - License not renewed for period of three years and that too in respect of commercial vehicle like truck - employer cannot wash his hands off responsibility of not checking up whether the driver has renewed Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/
8 license - Gross negligence on part of employees as insured in verifying driving license, Insurance Company not liable to pay compensation." 
U/sec 3 of M.V Act and also meaning and definition of 'Effective driving licence' viz a viz section 3, 4 and 5 of M.V Act, whereby the insurance company has done all its efforts in establishing the fact that there was a fundamental breach of policy condition. If a person drives the vehicle without a driving license or the owner allows the person to drive the vehicle without driving license there is a breach of section 3 of M.V Act which would no doubt make the owner liable for the consequences as per the M.V act and as per the section 181 of M.V Act.
27. In this case, as stated above petitioner has not proved that the rider of the motorcycle was having driving license at the time of accident. Therefore, the court has opinion that the rider of the motorcycle was not having driving license at the time of accident. There is fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the policy. Therefore, judgment in MFA No. 22781/2012 C/w MFA No.
22539/2012 (MV) in a case The Divisional Manager, Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Shri Arjun Datatray Gurav and another, wherein it is held that when there is fundamental breach of the policy condition the legibility fix on the insurance company. Therefore, this being the violation of the policy conditions while considering the liability. 
28. Further this court has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme court of India 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 932 in a case of Balu Krishna Chavan Vs. The Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. & others wherein held that if the liability of the insurance company is decided and they are held not to the liable, ordinarily, there shall be no direction to "pay and recover", Further in para No.8 held that hence, the only aspect for out consideration herein, is as to whether in the facts and circumstances of the present case, an order to direct the Insurance Company to "pay and recover", is required to be made. On this aspect, the law is well settled that if the liability of the Insurance Company is decided and they are held not to be liable, ordinarily, there shall be no direction to "pay and recover". 
However, in the facts and circumstances arising in each case, appropriate orders are required to be made by this court to meet the ends of justice. 
(emphasis supplied). 
Therefore, in view of the above dictum of the hon'ble Supreme court of India the principal of pay and recovery cannot be applies in the present case. Therefore, under such circumstances, it is the owner respondent No.2 is held liable to pay the compensation as awarded by the tribunal. The liability of the insurance company is hereby exonerated from the liability. 
29. INTEREST: As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%. By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand. Accordingly, issue No.2 is Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/
9 answered partly in the affirmative.
30. ISSUE No.3: In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER: 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs. 
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.4,97,085/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization. 
The respondent No.2 being the owner of the vehicle involved in an accident is personally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award. 
The liability of the respondent No.1 insurance company to pay the compensation to the petitioner is hereby exonerated. 
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 50% of amount shall be released in the name of petitioner along with interest thereon. 
 Remaining 50% of compensation amount of  petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years. 
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank. Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card. 
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal. 
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal. 
Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/
10 Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court. 
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-. 
Draw award accordingly.
